destinations.name: Guimaras
destinations.tagline: The island famous for the sweetest mangoes in the Philippines.
destinations.description: Guimaras is a small island province between Iloilo and Negros, best known for its exceptionally sweet carabao mangoes. White-sand coves, a centuries-old lighthouse, and a hilltop shrine with sweeping views make it an easy island escape. It is a popular day trip or weekend getaway from Iloilo City.
destinations.whyPopular: Its mangoes are reputedly among the sweetest in the world, and the island pairs that food fame with quiet beaches and historic sites. The Manggahan Festival every April or May celebrates the mango harvest.
destinations.howToGetThere: Take a 15-minute pump boat from Ortiz Wharf in Iloilo City to Jordan Wharf in Guimaras, then ride a tricycle or jeepney around the island.

places.name: Alubihod Beach
places.description: A quiet cove in Nueva Valencia with white sand, calm water, and island views. It is the island's most developed beach area, lined with small resorts.

places.name: Guisi Lighthouse
places.description: An 18th-century Spanish-era lighthouse standing on a cliff in Barangay Guisi. The short climb rewards visitors with wide views of the sea and the horizon.

places.name: Balaan Bukid Shrine
places.description: A hilltop shrine in Buenavista marked by a large white cross visible from Iloilo. The climb passes the Stations of the Cross and ends with a panoramic view of the Iloilo Strait.

places.name: Natago Beach Island Hopping
places.description: Pump boats from Alubihod visit nearby islets such as Natago Beach and Ave Maria Islet. Expect sandbars, snorkeling spots, and clear shallow water.

places.name: Mango Plantation Tour
places.description: Tour the mango orchards that made Guimaras famous and taste fresh carabao mangoes in season. Some farms let visitors pick fruit or buy by the kilo.

places.name: Pitstop Restaurant
places.description: A well-known stop in Buenavista famous for its mango pizza and mango-based dishes. It is the classic lunch break on any Guimaras road trip.

places.name: Raymen Beach Resort
places.description: A beachfront resort on Alubihod Beach with cottages, a pool, and direct sea access. It is one of the island's longest-running places to stay.

places.name: Trappist Monastery Shop
places.description: The Our Lady of the Philippines Trappist Monastery shop sells mango jams, preserves, and religious items made by the monks. It is the top pasalubong stop on the island.

places.name: Tricycle Day Tour
places.description: Tricycles are the main way to hop between beaches, the lighthouse, and the monastery. Drivers often double as informal tour guides for a fixed day rate.

places.name: Multicab Rental
places.description: Groups can hire a multicab or van with driver to circle the island's sights in one day. Hotels and the Jordan port area can arrange one on arrival.

transport.useCase: Getting to Guimaras from Iloilo City
transport.notes: Boats leave Ortiz Wharf every 15 to 30 minutes from early morning to late afternoon.

transport.useCase: Touring the island's beaches and landmarks
transport.notes: Agree on the route and price before starting; most drivers know the standard loop.

transport.useCase: Budget travel between Jordan, Buenavista, and Nueva Valencia
transport.notes: Public jeepneys run set routes between the main towns during daytime.

transport.useCase: Independent exploring for confident riders
transport.notes: Available in Jordan and Nueva Valencia; bring a valid driver's license.

destinations.name: Malapascua
destinations.tagline: The only place in the world where thresher sharks are seen almost daily.
destinations.description: Malapascua is a small island off northern Cebu famous for Monad Shoal, where thresher sharks rise to cleaning stations at dawn. Beyond the sharks, it offers white-sand beaches, wreck dives, and a laid-back island scene. Divers and beach lovers travel here from around the world.
destinations.whyPopular: It is the only dive site in the world with near-daily thresher shark sightings, plus the nearby Gato Island sea snake sanctuary. The famous Kalanggaman sandbar is an easy day trip from here.
destinations.howToGetThere: Take a bus or van from Cebu City to Maya Port in Daanbantayan (3 to 4 hours), then a 30-minute public boat to Malapascua.

places.name: Monad Shoal
places.description: A submerged plateau where thresher sharks visit cleaning stations at sunrise. Dawn dives here are the island's signature experience for certified divers.

places.name: Bounty Beach
places.description: The island's main white-sand beach, lined with resorts, dive shops, and bars. It faces west, so sunsets here are a nightly event.

places.name: Gato Island
places.description: A small rocky islet and marine reserve known for whitetip sharks, sea snakes, and a swim-through tunnel. It is a favorite second dive after Monad Shoal.

places.name: Thresher Shark Dawn Dive
places.description: Join a 5 a.m. dive briefing and descend to Monad Shoal as the thresher sharks arrive. Open Water certification and good buoyancy control are required.

places.name: Kalanggaman Sandbar Day Trip
places.description: Speedboats run day trips to the famous Kalanggaman sandbar, about an hour away. Trips usually include lunch, snorkeling stops, and beach time.

places.name: Ging-Ging's Restaurant
places.description: A long-running beachfront spot serving Filipino dishes, fresh seafood, and breakfast sets. It is a favorite among divers refueling between dives.

places.name: Ocean Vida Beach Resort
places.description: A beachfront resort on Bounty Beach with its own dive center, pool, and restaurant. It is popular with divers who want everything in one place.

places.name: Tepanee Beach Resort
places.description: A quieter resort on the north side of the island with cottages set in tropical gardens. It suits travelers who want calm after the dive boats leave.

places.name: Bounty Beach Souvenir Stalls
places.description: Dive shops and stalls along Bounty Beach sell thresher shark shirts, rash guards, and local handicrafts. Prices are fixed in some shops and haggle-friendly in others.

places.name: Motorbike Rental
places.description: Rent a motorbike to reach quiet coves and viewpoints on the island's far side. The island is small, so a half day covers the full loop.

transport.useCase: Crossing from Maya Port to Malapascua
transport.notes: Boats leave when full from early morning to late afternoon; the trip takes about 30 minutes.

transport.useCase: Faster crossing or group transfers on your own schedule
transport.notes: Resorts and Maya Port operators can arrange private boats, useful for late arrivals.

transport.useCase: Getting from Cebu City to Maya Port
transport.notes: Ceres buses and vans leave from Cebu North Bus Terminal; the ride takes 3 to 4 hours.

transport.useCase: Short rides around the island
transport.notes: Motorcycle taxis wait near the village center and Bounty Beach.

destinations.name: Kalanggaman Island
destinations.tagline: A postcard sandbar floating between Cebu and Leyte.
destinations.description: Kalanggaman Island is a tiny uninhabited island off Palompon, Leyte, famous for its long white sandbar stretching into turquoise water. There are no hotels or restaurants, only clear water, snorkeling, and camping under the stars. It is one of the most photographed beaches in the Visayas.
destinations.whyPopular: The sandbar looks like a scene from a travel magazine, and the surrounding reef offers easy snorkeling. Overnight camping lets visitors have the island nearly to themselves.
destinations.howToGetThere: Travel to Palompon, Leyte, register at the tourism office, then take a pump boat to the island (about 1 hour).

places.name: Kalanggaman Sandbar
places.description: The island's famous white sandbar extends hundreds of meters into clear blue water. Walk its full length at low tide for the classic panoramic photos.

places.name: Kalanggaman Reef
places.description: Coral gardens and reef slopes surround the island with decent visibility on calm days. Expect small reef fish, corals, and occasional sea turtles.

places.name: Kalanggaman Island Campsite
places.description: Overnight guests pitch tents in the designated camping area or rent tents from the tourism office. Falling asleep to the waves with almost no light pollution is the main draw.

places.name: Island Kayaking
places.description: Rent a kayak and paddle around the island or out toward the sandbar tip. The water is usually calmest in the morning.

places.name: Beach Volleyball
places.description: Join pickup beach volleyball games on the main beach, a favorite pastime of overnight campers. Equipment is sometimes available from the tourism staff.

places.name: Palompon Public Market
places.description: Stock up on grilled food, rice meals, and snacks at Palompon Public Market before boarding the boat. Most visitors bring all their food since the island has no restaurants.

places.name: Palompon Port Carinderias
places.description: Small carinderias near Palompon Port serve hot Filipino meals to day-trippers before or after the crossing. A practical breakfast stop before the early boat.

places.name: Kalanggaman Souvenir Stall
places.description: A small stall near the island's arrival area sells Kalanggaman shirts and trinkets. The Palompon tourism office also stocks official merchandise.

places.name: Island Walk
places.description: The island is tiny enough to circle on foot in under an hour. All movement on the island is by walking along the beach and trails.

places.name: Pump Boat Crossing
places.description: Pump boats are the only way on and off the island, arranged through the Palompon tourism office. Boats can be shared with other groups to split the cost.

transport.useCase: The only way to reach Kalanggaman Island
transport.notes: Book through the Palompon tourism office; sharing a boat with other groups lowers the cost.

transport.useCase: Getting to Palompon from Tacloban or Ormoc
transport.notes: Vans leave regularly in the morning; the ride from Ormoc takes about 2 hours.

transport.useCase: Moving around Palompon town and to the port
transport.notes: The tourism office, market, and port are all within a short tricycle ride.

transport.useCase: Island entrance and conservation fee
transport.notes: Paid at the Palompon tourism office; rates differ for day visitors and overnight campers.

destinations.name: Bacolod
destinations.tagline: The City of Smiles, home of chicken inasal and the MassKara Festival.
destinations.description: Bacolod is the capital of Negros Occidental and one of the friendliest cities in the Philippines. It is famous for chicken inasal, sweet piaya, and the MassKara Festival every October. The Ruins in nearby Talisay and the highland resort of Mambukal round out its attractions.
destinations.whyPopular: Food travelers come for the inasal crawl and Calea cakes, while culture seekers time visits for MassKara's street dancing. It is also the gateway to Negros island adventures.
destinations.howToGetThere: Fly to Bacolod-Silay Airport (about 1 hour from Manila), then take a shuttle or taxi to the city. Ferries also connect Bacolod to Iloilo in about 1 hour.

places.name: The Ruins
places.description: The skeletal remains of a grand 1900s sugar baron mansion in Talisay, lit beautifully at night. It is the most photographed landmark in Negros.

places.name: San Sebastian Cathedral
places.description: A 19th-century stone church in the city center and the seat of the Bacolod diocese. Its coral-stone facade is a quiet contrast to the busy plaza outside.

places.name: Negros Museum
places.description: A museum of Negrense history, art, and the sugar industry housed in a former agricultural building. Good for a quick culture stop between food trips.

places.name: MassKara Festival
places.description: Every October, dancers in colorful smiling masks parade through the streets for MassKara. Book hotels early, since the city fills up for the festival week.

places.name: Mambukal Resort Day Trip
places.description: Mambukal Resort in Murcia offers hot sulfur springs, waterfalls, and forest trails about an hour from the city. It is the classic Bacolod weekend escape.

places.name: Manokan Country
places.description: A row of open-air stalls grilling chicken inasal over charcoal near SM City Bacolod. This is the pilgrimage site for the city's signature dish.

places.name: Aida's Chicken
places.description: Aida's is one of the original inasal houses, famous for its paa and pecho with chicken oil rice. Expect a line at peak meal times.

places.name: Calea Pastries
places.description: Calea is beloved for its cakes, especially the chocolate and mango variants, at prices far below Manila cafes. Boxes of cake are a standard pasalubong.

places.name: Seda Capitol Central
places.description: A modern business hotel beside Ayala Malls Capitol Central with a rooftop pool. It is a convenient base for both business and leisure trips.

places.name: BongBong's Piaya Pasalubong
places.description: BongBong's is the go-to brand for piaya, napoleones, and other Negrense sweets. Branches across the city make last-minute pasalubong runs easy.

places.name: City Jeepney
places.description: Jeepneys cover the main routes across the city for a low flat fare. They are the cheapest way to move between malls, the plaza, and Manokan Country.

transport.useCase: Comfortable rides around the city and to the airport
transport.notes: Grab operates in Bacolod; airport taxis charge fixed rates to the city.

transport.useCase: Cheapest way to travel set city routes
transport.notes: Routes are posted on the windshield; ask the driver if unsure.

transport.useCase: Short trips and areas off jeepney routes
transport.notes: Agree on the fare before boarding, especially at night.

transport.useCase: Getting between Bacolod-Silay Airport and the city
transport.notes: Shuttle vans wait outside the arrival area and leave when full.

destinations.name: Apo Island
destinations.tagline: Swim with sea turtles in a community-run marine sanctuary.
destinations.description: Apo Island is a small volcanic island off Dauin, Negros Oriental, wrapped in one of the country's oldest community-managed marine sanctuaries. Green sea turtles graze in the shallows while coral gardens teem with fish. It works as a day trip from Dumaguete or a quiet overnight stay.
destinations.whyPopular: Turtle sightings are almost guaranteed on a single snorkel, and the sanctuary model is a global example of community conservation. The island stays low-key, with no cars and few crowds.
destinations.howToGetThere: From Dumaguete, ride to Malatapay Port in Zamboanguita (30 minutes), then take a 30-minute boat to Apo Island.

places.name: Apo Island Marine Sanctuary
places.description: The protected reef in front of the village where turtles, corals, and schools of fish thrive. A guide and sanctuary fee are required to snorkel here.

places.name: Chapel Point
places.description: A coral-covered point on the island's south side with turtles, bumphead parrotfish, and occasional reef sharks. A favorite for both snorkelers and divers.

places.name: Lighthouse Viewpoint
places.description: A short hike up to the old lighthouse offers a full view of the island and the sea toward Negros. Best visited late in the afternoon for softer light.

places.name: Sea Turtle Snorkeling
places.description: Float over the sanctuary reef as green sea turtles surface for air around you. Guides know the cleaning spots where turtles linger longest.

places.name: Apo Island Scuba Diving
places.description: Dive sites like Coconut Point and Rock Point West offer drift dives along coral walls. Currents can be strong, so they suit experienced divers.

places.name: Liberty's Lodge Restaurant
places.description: Liberty's Lodge runs a simple restaurant serving Filipino meals and fresh seafood to guests and walk-ins. Meals are hearty after a morning in the water.

places.name: Liberty's Lodge
places.description: A long-running lodge on the beach with simple rooms and a dive shop attached. It is the classic budget-friendly base on the island.

places.name: Apo Island Beach Resort
places.description: Apo Island Beach Resort offers fan and air-conditioned rooms steps from the sanctuary. Its restaurant serves guests throughout the day.

places.name: Sanctuary Souvenir Stalls
places.description: Small stalls near the sanctuary entrance sell turtle-themed shirts, shell crafts, and handmade jewelry. Buying here supports the island community directly.

places.name: Island Walking Trails
places.description: There are no motorized vehicles on the island, so everywhere is reached on foot. Trails connect the village, beaches, and the lighthouse viewpoint.

transport.useCase: Crossing from Malatapay Port to Apo Island
transport.notes: Boats leave Malatapay in the morning and return mid-afternoon; schedules depend on demand.

transport.useCase: Getting from Dumaguete to Malatapay Port
transport.notes: The ride to Zamboanguita takes about 30 minutes; tricycles can be hired for a round trip.

transport.useCase: Budget ride from Dauin or Zamboanguita to the port
transport.notes: Motorcycle taxis are easy to find along the Dumaguete to Zamboanguita highway.

transport.useCase: Reaching dive sites around the island
transport.notes: Dive shops include boat transfers in their dive packages.

destinations.name: Samal Island
destinations.tagline: Davao's island playground of luxury resorts and bat caves.
destinations.description: The Island Garden City of Samal sits just off Davao City, minutes by ferry but worlds apart in pace. It mixes high-end resorts like Pearl Farm with public beaches, a giant bat colony, and quiet fishing villages. It is Davao's default weekend escape.
destinations.whyPopular: Pearl Farm put Samal on the luxury map, while the Monfort Bat Sanctuary holds a world record for the largest fruit bat colony. The island is close enough for easy Davao City day trips.
destinations.howToGetThere: Take a ferry from Sasa Wharf in Davao City to Babak Port, or ride the Island City Express bus which crosses by RoRo ferry (about 45 minutes total).

places.name: Pearl Farm Beach Resort
places.description: The iconic overwater-cottage resort on a private islet off Samal. Day tour guests can use the pools, beach, and restaurants with a prior booking.

places.name: Monfort Bat Sanctuary
places.description: Home to around two million fruit bats, recognized by Guinness as the largest colony of its kind. Guided walks pass viewing decks at dusk when the bats stream out.

places.name: Vanishing Island
places.description: A sandbar off Barangay Tambo that appears and disappears with the tide. Boats from the mainland coast make the short crossing at low tide.

places.name: Coral Garden Snorkeling
places.description: Snorkel the Coral Garden marine sanctuary with its giant clams and coral formations. Local guides provide gear and know the calmest entry points.

places.name: Samal Island Hopping Tour
places.description: Boat tours link Kaputian Beach, the Vanishing Island, and snorkeling stops in one trip. Most tours leave in the morning and return by mid-afternoon.

places.name: Kaputian Seafood Grills
places.description: Grill restaurants along the Kaputian coast serve fresh catch, kinilaw, and grilled squid. Pick your fish from the display and have it cooked to order.

places.name: Discovery Samal
places.description: Discovery Samal is a newer upscale resort with a long beachfront, pools, and modern rooms. It targets travelers who want Pearl Farm-style comfort on the main island.

places.name: Costa Marina Beach Resort
places.description: A mid-range beach resort in Babak with a wide beach, pool, and function halls. A practical pick for families arriving on the Babak ferry.

places.name: Babak Public Market
places.description: Babak Public Market sells fresh seafood, fruits, and local snacks near the port. It is the best place to buy ingredients or cheap pasalubong.

places.name: Samal Souvenir Shops
places.description: Souvenir stalls near the main resorts and ports sell Samal shirts, pearl accessories, and woven crafts. Resort gift shops carry higher-end local products.

places.name: Habal-habal Rides
places.description: Motorcycle taxis are the fastest way to move between Samal's spread-out beaches and attractions. Agree on the fare before hopping on.

transport.useCase: Crossing from Sasa Wharf in Davao City to Babak
transport.notes: Ferries run frequently from early morning to evening; the crossing takes about 15 minutes.

transport.useCase: Direct bus from Davao City into Samal via RoRo
transport.notes: Buses board the RoRo ferry with passengers, so there is no transfer needed.

transport.useCase: Getting between beaches, resorts, and the bat sanctuary
transport.notes: Drivers gather at the ports and main road junctions; negotiate round trips.

transport.useCase: Group tours covering the island in one day
transport.notes: Resorts and Davao City operators offer vans with drivers familiar with Samal.

destinations.name: Mati, Davao Oriental
destinations.tagline: Dahican Beach, skimboarding capital and turtle nesting haven.
destinations.description: Mati is the capital of Davao Oriental, facing the Pacific with the long crescent of Dahican Beach. It is the skimboarding capital of the Philippines and a nesting site for sea turtles. Pujada Bay, one of the country's most beautiful bays, frames the horizon.
destinations.whyPopular: Dahican's consistent shore break made it the birthplace of Philippine skimboarding, and Amihan sa Dahican hosts international skim events. The Sleeping Dinosaur viewpoint is one of Mindanao's most photographed lookouts.
destinations.howToGetThere: Buses run from Davao City to Mati (about 4 to 5 hours). From Mati city proper, tricycles reach Dahican Beach in 15 minutes.

places.name: Dahican Beach
places.description: A 7-kilometer crescent of white sand facing the Pacific, famous for skimboarding and surfing. The beach stays relatively uncrowded outside event season.

places.name: Sleeping Dinosaur Viewpoint
places.description: A rock formation on Pujada Bay that looks like a dinosaur lying in the water. The viewpoint above it offers the classic photo of the bay.

places.name: Subangan Museum
places.description: A natural history museum in Mati city housing the skeleton of a sperm whale found in the area. Exhibits cover Davao Oriental's marine and forest life.

places.name: Dahican Skimboarding
places.description: Rent a skimboard or take a lesson on Dahican's shore break, where the sport took root in the Philippines. Amihan sa Dahican runs lessons and hosts competitions.

places.name: Turtle Hatchling Release
places.description: Watch hatchling releases at Dahican during nesting season, usually with guidance from local conservation groups. Releases often happen at sunset.

places.name: Dahican Seafood Grills
places.description: Beachfront grills along Dahican serve fresh tuna, squid, and kinilaw at local prices. Many resorts also cook the day's catch for guests.

places.name: Mati Baywalk Food Stalls
places.description: Evening food stalls at Mati Baywalk offer barbecue, street food, and shakes with a view of Pujada Bay. A favorite hangout for locals after sunset.

places.name: Dahican Surf Resort
places.description: Dahican Surf Resort sits right on the sand with cottages, a restaurant, and skimboard rentals. It is the social hub of the Dahican skim scene.

places.name: Mati Pasalubong Center
places.description: Shops in Mati city sell Davao Oriental coffee, cacao products, and woven souvenirs. Dahican stalls add surf-themed shirts and trinkets.

places.name: Tricycle Rides
places.description: Tricycles connect Mati city, Dahican Beach, and the baywalk viewpoints. For the Sleeping Dinosaur, hire one for a half-day round trip.

transport.useCase: Getting from Davao City to Mati
transport.notes: Bachelor Express and other buses leave Ecoland Terminal; the ride takes 4 to 5 hours.

transport.useCase: Getting from Mati city to Dahican Beach
transport.notes: The beach is about 15 minutes from the city proper.

transport.useCase: Reaching the Sleeping Dinosaur and other viewpoints
transport.notes: Hire for a half day so the driver waits while you explore.

transport.useCase: Group trips covering Dahican, the museum, and viewpoints
transport.notes: Mati operators offer vans with drivers who know the coastal routes.

destinations.name: Lake Sebu
destinations.tagline: Seven waterfalls, a zipline, and the culture of the T'boli.
destinations.description: Lake Sebu is a highland town in South Cotabato built around a serene lake and the ancestral land of the T'boli people. The Seven Falls, one of which is crossed by a high zipline, are the headline attraction. T'nalak weaving and lotus-filled waters give the town a distinct cultural flavor.
destinations.whyPopular: The Seven Falls zipline is among the highest in Southeast Asia, and the T'boli's t'nalak cloth is a treasured Philippine textile. The lake cruise at sunrise, past lotus pads and fish cages, is quietly magical.
destinations.howToGetThere: From General Santos City, take a bus or van to Surallah, then a jeepney or habal-habal up to Lake Sebu (about 2 hours total).

places.name: Seven Falls
places.description: A series of seven waterfalls in the rainforest, with the first two reachable by a short trek. Hikong Bente, the tallest, is crossed by the famous zipline.

places.name: Punta Isla
places.description: Punta Isla sits on a small island in the lake with floating cottages, a restaurant, and gardens. It is the classic lunch stop for its tilapia dishes.

places.name: T'boli Museum
places.description: A small museum of T'boli artifacts, brass work, and musical instruments in the town center. It gives context to the weaving and culture seen around the lake.

places.name: Seven Falls Zipline
places.description: Ride one of the highest ziplines in Southeast Asia over Hikong Bente falls at 180 meters up. The tandem ride gives a full aerial view of the falls and forest.

places.name: Sunrise Lake Cruise
places.description: Cruise the lake at sunrise past lotus flowers, fish cages, and stilt houses. Pump boats leave from the Punta Isla area and nearby docks.

places.name: Lakeside Tilapia Restaurants
places.description: Lakeside restaurants serve the town's famous tilapia, raised in the lake's fish cages, grilled or cooked in coconut milk. Punta Isla's restaurant is the best known.

places.name: Punta Isla Lake Resort
places.description: Stay in floating cottages or lakeside rooms right on the water with sunrise views. The resort's restaurant and gardens make it a full experience.

places.name: Lang Dulay T'nalak Weaving Center
places.description: The Lang Dulay T'nalak Weaving Center honors the National Living Treasure weaver and sells authentic t'nalak cloth. Weavers demonstrate the traditional dyeing and weaving process.

places.name: Lake Sebu Souvenir Shops
places.description: Stalls near the lake and Seven Falls sell brass bells, beaded accessories, and T'boli-inspired crafts. Prices are generally fixed and fair.

places.name: Habal-habal Rides
places.description: Motorcycle taxis handle the steep roads to the Seven Falls and weaving center. Drivers wait at the town terminal and major junctions.

places.name: Lakeside Tricycles
places.description: Tricycles cover the flat lakeside roads between resorts, restaurants, and the town proper. They are the easiest option for short hops.

transport.useCase: Getting from General Santos City to Surallah
transport.notes: Buses and vans leave GenSan regularly; the ride to Surallah takes about 1 hour.

transport.useCase: Climbing from Surallah to Lake Sebu town
transport.notes: Jeepneys run the uphill route throughout the day.

transport.useCase: Reaching the Seven Falls and weaving center
transport.notes: The standard ride for the steep roads; drivers wait at the terminal.

transport.useCase: Lake cruises and crossing to lakeside resorts
transport.notes: Arrange through resorts or the docks near Punta Isla.

destinations.name: Bislig
destinations.tagline: Home of Tinuy-an Falls, the Niagara of the Philippines.
destinations.description: Bislig is a coastal city in Surigao del Sur best known for Tinuy-an Falls, a wide multi-tiered cascade often called the Niagara of the Philippines. The nearby Enchanted River in Hinatuan adds another must-see stop. Bislig works as a base for exploring the Pacific coast of Surigao.
destinations.whyPopular: Tinuy-an's curtain of water and its bamboo raft ride under the falls are bucket-list experiences. The Enchanted River's impossibly blue water, a short drive away, completes the trip.
destinations.howToGetThere: Buses run from Davao City or Butuan to Bislig (4 to 6 hours). From Bislig city, habal-habal or vans reach Tinuy-an Falls in about 30 minutes.

places.name: Tinuy-an Falls
places.description: A 95-meter-wide, multi-tiered waterfall cascading into a turquoise basin. Bamboo rafts take visitors right under the curtain of water for the full experience.

places.name: Hinatuan Enchanted River
places.description: The famous deep-blue river in nearby Hinatuan where fish feeding happens at noon daily. Swimming is limited to a designated area to protect the spring.

places.name: Bislig Baywalk
places.description: Bislig Baywalk is an evening promenade along the coast with food stalls and sea views. Locals gather here at sunset for snacks and the ocean breeze.

places.name: Tinuy-an Bamboo Raft Ride
places.description: Ride a bamboo raft to the base of Tinuy-an Falls and feel the waterfall's spray up close. Life vests are provided and the ride takes about 15 minutes.

places.name: Enchanted River Swim
places.description: Swim in the designated area of the Enchanted River's impossibly clear blue water. The daily fish feeding at noon is the highlight to time your visit around.

places.name: Tinuy-an Jump-off Carinderias
places.description: Carinderias near the Tinuy-an Falls jump-off serve rice meals and grilled seafood to day-trippers. Bislig city's eateries offer the same at local prices.

places.name: Baywalk Evening Food Stalls
places.description: Evening stalls at Bislig Baywalk sell barbecue, grilled tuna, and refreshments by the sea. It doubles as dinner and sunset viewing.

places.name: Paper Country Inn
places.description: Paper Country Inn is a well-known Bislig hotel with comfortable rooms and a central location. It is a convenient base for falls and river day trips.

places.name: Bislig Pasalubong Center
places.description: Pasalubong centers in Bislig city sell Surigao del Sur coffee, banana chips, and local sweets. Falls-side stalls add Tinuy-an souvenir shirts.

places.name: Habal-habal to the Falls
places.description: Motorcycle taxis are the standard ride from Bislig city to Tinuy-an Falls and other outlying spots. Arrange a round trip with waiting time.

transport.useCase: Getting to Bislig from Davao City or Butuan
transport.notes: Bachelor Express and other lines serve Bislig; the ride takes 4 to 6 hours.

transport.useCase: Reaching Tinuy-an Falls from Bislig city
transport.notes: Drivers wait at the falls while you explore; agree on waiting time upfront.

transport.useCase: Short trips within Bislig city
transport.notes: Tricycles cover the city center, baywalk, and market area.

transport.useCase: Group day trips to the falls and Enchanted River
transport.notes: Vans can combine Tinuy-an Falls and Hinatuan's Enchanted River in one day.
